title.en: Find the force per unit length between parallel currents.

say.en: Two wires carrying current in the same direction pull towards each other. This small force is so reliable that for decades it was used to define the ampere. In this lesson: Find the force per unit length between parallel currents.
Define one ampere.

body.en: Wire a, carrying $I_a$, produces $B = \mu_0I_a/2\pi d$ at wire b, a distance d away. Wire b, carrying $I_b$, therefore feels a *force* per unit length $f = \mu_0I_aI_b/2\pi d$. Currents in the same direction attract; currents in opposite directions repel. This is the reverse of electric charges, where like charges repel.
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ತಂತಿ ಇನ್ನೊಂದರ ಕಾಂತಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಮೀಟರ್‌ಗೆ ಬಲ f = μ₀I_aI_b/2πd. ಒಂದೇ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳು ಆಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನವು ವಿಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

narration.en: Each wire sits in the other's magnetic field, so the force per metre is mu nought I a I b by 2 pi d. Parallel currents attract and antiparallel currents repel.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ತಂತಿ ಇನ್ನೊಂದರ ಕಾಂತಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ಮೀಟರ್‌ಗೆ ಬಲ f = μ₀I_aI_b/2πd. ಒಂದೇ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನ ಪ್ರವಾಹಗಳು ಆಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ವಿರುದ್ಧ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನವು ವಿಕರ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: Each wire sits in the other's magnetic field, so the force per metre is mu nought I a I b by 2 pi d. Parallel currents attract and antiparallel currents repel. f equals micro 0I aI b over 2 pi d.

say.en: Same direction: attract.
Opposite directions: repel.

title.en: On the board: force between parallel currents

narration.en: Two long parallel wires, a distance d apart, carry currents I_a and I_b in the same direction. Wire a makes a field μ₀I_a/2πd at wire b, pointing into the page there. So wire b feels a force I_b L B_a towards wire a: parallel currents attract, opposite currents repel. The ampere: 1 A in each of two wires 1 m apart in vacuum gives a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ newton per metre. Example: 10 A and 5 A, 4 cm apart, give f = 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 50 / 0.04 = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ newton per metre.

say.en: Two long parallel wires, a distance d apart, carry currents I_a and I_b in the same direction.
Wire a makes a field μ₀I_a/2πd at wire b, pointing into the page there.
So wire b feels a force I_b L B_a towards wire a: parallel currents attract, opposite currents repel.
The ampere: 1 A in each of two wires 1 m apart in vacuum gives a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ newton per metre.
Example: 10 A and 5 A, 4 cm apart, give f = 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 50 / 0.04 = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ newton per metre.

Two long parallel wires, a distance d apart, carry currents I a and I b in the same direction. Wire a makes a field micro 0I a over 2 pi d at wire b, pointing into the page there. So wire b feels a force I b L B a towards wire a: parallel currents attract, opposite currents repel. The ampere: 1 A in each of two wires 1 metre apart in vacuum gives a force of 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 newton per metre. Example: 10 A and 5 A, 4 centimetres apart, give f equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times 50 divided by 0.04 equals 2.5 times 10 to the power minus 4 newton per metre.

narration.en: Wire 1 makes a field B = μ0 I1 / 2πd at wire 2, and that field pushes on the current in wire 2. The force per metre is f = μ0 I1 I2 / 2πd. Currents in the same direction attract; opposite directions repel. One ampere is the current that gives 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre for wires 1 m apart.

say.en: Wire 1 makes a field B equals micro 0 I1 divided by 2 pi d at wire 2, and that field pushes on the current in wire 2. The force per metre is f equals micro 0 I1 I2 divided by 2 pi d. Currents in the same direction attract; opposite directions repel. One ampere is the current that gives 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 newtons per metre for wires 1 metre apart.

body.en: One *ampere* is that steady current which, flowing in two very long, straight, parallel conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 m apart in vacuum, produces between them a force of 2 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre of length. The coulomb then follows: 1 C = 1 A × 1 s.

problem.en: Two long parallel wires 5 cm apart carry 10 A and 20 A in the same direction. Find the force per metre between them.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Two long parallel wires 5 cm apart carry 10 A and 20 A in the same direction. Find the force per metre between them.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Two long parallel wires 5 centimetres apart carry 10 A and 20 A in the same direction. Find the force per metre between them.
f equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times I 1I 2 over d.
f equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times 10 times 20 over 0.05.
f equals 8 times 10 to the power minus 4 newtons m to the power minus 1, attractive.
So the answer is 8 times 10 to the power minus 4 newtons per metre, attractive.

problem.en: Two long parallel wires 1 m apart carry equal currents and attract with 8 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre. Find the current.

steps.en: I = 2 A, in the same direction in both wires.

answer.en: 2 A in each wire, same direction

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Two long parallel wires 1 m apart carry equal currents and attract with 8 × 10⁻⁷ N per metre. Find the current.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Two long parallel wires 1 metre apart carry equal currents and attract with 8 times 10 to the power minus 7 newtons per metre. Find the current.
f equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 I squared/d.
8 times 10 to the power minus 7 equals 2 times 10 to the power minus 7 times I squared/1, so I squared equals 4.
I equals 2 A, in the same direction in both wires.
So the answer is 2 A in each wire, same direction.

heading.en: Opposite rules for currents and charges

body.en: Like charges repel, but like (parallel) currents attract. Unlike charges attract, but unlike (antiparallel) currents repel.

narration.en: Opposite rules for currents and charges. Like charges repel, but like (parallel) currents attract. Unlike charges attract, but unlike (antiparallel) currents repel.

mnemonic.en: Charges: like repel. Currents: like attract.

say.en: Opposite rules for currents and charges. Like charges repel, but like parallel currents attract. Unlike charges attract, but unlike antiparallel currents repel.
